register: Polite; the default in conversation with strangers and in writing aimed at readers.

examples.japanese: 毎日コーヒーを飲みます。
examples.reading: まいにちコーヒーをのみます。
にほんごをべんきょうします。
あした、がっこうにいきます。
examples.gloss: I will go to school tomorrow.

usage: Adds politeness and nothing else. The meaning of the sentence does not change.
A ます-form has its own small paradigm: ません, ました, ませんでした, ましょう, まして. Nothing else attaches to it, so there is no 食べますたい and no 食べますない.
Put the other suffixes before ます: 食べさせます, 食べられます. たい stays before です instead: 食べたいです.

compare.difference: です does the same job for い-adjectives and nouns. ます is only for verbs.

compare.label: Plain form
compare.difference: Plain forms (食べる) are for friends, family and for clauses inside a longer sentence. Even in a polite sentence, a clause in the middle is usually plain.
